title: HeyGen: the AI video company built by a man who hated cameras
disclosure: AFFILIATE LINK IN DESCRIPTION. AI VOICE

scenes.label: JUNE 2026
scenes.narration: June 2026. An AI video company announced that it now earns over 200 million dollars a year in recurring revenue. And it says it barely burned any cash to get there.

title: NO CAMERA.
NO STUDIO.
scenes.subtitle: THE HEYGEN STORY
scenes.narration: The company is HeyGen. It makes videos where nobody has to stand in front of a camera. Here is how it happened.

scenes.label: SNAPCHAT
scenes.narration: It starts with Joshua Xu. He studied computer science at Carnegie Mellon, then spent six years as an engineer at Snapchat, working on machine learning and camera technology.

scenes.label: SHENZHEN
scenes.narration: In December 2020, during the pandemic, Joshua and his co-founder Wayne Liang started a company in Shenzhen, China. Its first name was Surreal.

scenes.label: R&D LAB
scenes.narration: Joshua has said he never felt comfortable on camera. So the idea was simple: let AI make the video, so people can stay off camera.

scenes.label: LOS ANGELES
scenes.narration: Later, under the name Movio, the company moved its headquarters to Los Angeles. On July 29, 2022, it launched its product.

scenes.label: SERVER ROOM
scenes.narration: The company says it took just 178 days to reach one million dollars in yearly recurring revenue. By day 217, it was ramen profitable.

scenes.label: TEAM KITCHEN
scenes.narration: Ramen profitable means earning just enough to pay the bills and eat cheap noodles. For a young AI startup, that is a big deal.

scenes.label: BRAND ROOM
scenes.narration: In April 2023, Movio became HeyGen. The new name came with a bigger goal: not just talking presenters, but a full AI video platform.
But growth brought trouble. HeyGen was a US company with roots in China, at a tense time between Washington and Beijing. American lawmakers started asking questions.
So the founders made a hard choice. They asked their Chinese investors to sell their shares to US investors, and the Shenzhen company was dissolved.

scenes.label: DEAL ROOM
scenes.narration: It worked. In June 2024, HeyGen raised 60 million dollars in a round led by Benchmark, at a valuation of about 500 million dollars.
Then the curve went almost straight up. The company says its yearly recurring revenue roughly doubled in eight months, passing 200 million dollars in June 2026.

scenes.label: TODAY
scenes.narration: Today HeyGen says more than 30 million people in 196 countries have used it, from solo creators to big companies.

scenes.label: HOW TO USE IT
scenes.caption: SCRIPT → AVATAR → VIDEO
scenes.narration: So how can you use it? Type a script, pick an AI avatar, and HeyGen turns it into a talking video. It can also translate videos into other languages.

scenes.label: FREE PLAN
scenes.narration: The free plan lets you make up to three videos a month, in 720p with a watermark. That is enough to test it before you pay anything.
